summary: Pandemic Studios' World War II open-world action game and its mobile tie-in.

entries.title: The Saboteur

emulation.notes: Use the PC version natively with community-known compatibility settings where required.

primary.why: The Saboteur released for Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360 in December 2009. Windows is the highest-fidelity and most flexible route for the full open-world game.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version natively with compatibility fixes if needed; use PS3 or Xbox 360 only for original-console comparison.

all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity and most flexible route.
skip: lower practical fidelity than Windows and no sourced content advantage.
skip: lower practical fidelity than Windows and no sourced content advantage.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive content requires a secondary route; Windows is the fidelity pick.

entries.remaster_caveats: No later remaster is documented in the cited public source; the PC release may need compatibility handling on modern systems.

entries.title: The Saboteur (mobile)
entries.definitive_edition: iOS mobile release for archival purposes

emulation.emulator: Original mobile hardware or preserved app environment
emulation.notes: Use only legally retained mobile installs or documentation if the app is no longer obtainable.

primary.why: The mobile tie-in to The Saboteur released for BlackBerry in January 2010 and iOS in March 2010. iOS is the more practical archival primary route, though normal modern storefront availability is not guaranteed.
primary.how_to_play: Preserve through legally retained iOS/BlackBerry installs or archival footage; do not treat this as a substitute for the full 2009 game.

all_releases.reason: primary: practical archival route for the mobile version.
skip: older mobile route and no sourced content advantage over iOS archival access.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: This is a separate mobile tie-in, not a port of the full open-world game.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile tie-in availability is preservation-sensitive; no modern remaster is documented in the cited public source.
